query: What product attributes are associated with higher satisfaction scores?

per_column.name: flavor_taste_quality
per_column.rationale: Positive/mixed/negative taste categories are interpretable, well-separated attribute segments that can be compared against satisfaction.

per_column.name: flavor_intensity_match
per_column.rationale: just_right/too_weak/too_strong is a clear ordinal-ish attribute segmentation, though heavy NULL (3427) weakens some cells.

per_column.name: product_quality_consistency
per_column.rationale: consistent vs batch_defect vs declined are interpretable quality categories groupable against satisfaction.

per_column.name: expectation_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Boolean whether product met expectations; clean well-populated split strongly relatable to satisfaction.

per_column.name: product_defect_mention
per_column.rationale: Interpretable binary defect flag; reasonably populated minority (1017) allows comparison.

per_column.name: product_efficacy
per_column.rationale: effective/partially/ineffective is a clear ordinal attribute segment comparable to satisfaction.

per_column.name: adverse_health_reaction
per_column.rationale: Interpretable but near-constant (149 true / 9851 false); too rare to draw robust comparisons, borderline uninformative.

per_column.name: repeat_purchase_intent
per_column.rationale: Repeat-purchase intent is essentially a downstream proxy of satisfaction rather than an external product attribute; largely restates the focus.

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: Well-separated, human-readable category segmentation ideal for grouping satisfaction by product type.

per_column.name: use_case_fit
per_column.rationale: Interpretable usage-context segments (daily_staple, gifting, dietary_need) support meaningful satisfaction comparisons.

per_column.name: convenience_availability
per_column.rationale: Binary convenience attribute; interpretable and adequately populated for comparison.

judge.rationale: Most added columns are genuine external product attributes with interpretable, well-separated categories that a human can group satisfaction by, directly serving the query. flavor_taste_quality, product_category, use_case_fit, efficacy, expectation_mismatch and quality_consistency are strong segmentation variables. Weaknesses: repeat_purchase_intent is a satisfaction proxy (restatement) rather than an attribute, and adverse_health_reaction is near-constant and thus weakly informative. Overall a strong, mostly non-mechanical set supporting interpretable relationship discovery.
